classification.difficultyReason: Model the triple overlap through its equality with the complement of folk, then combine the remaining total with a strict inequality and non-negative integer counts to determine the requested intersection.

content.prompt:
The 28 students in a class all buy music CDs. The categories they choose are rock ($R$), folk ($F$) and classical ($C$). One student buys classical CDs only. Nine students buy folk CDs only and five students buy rock CDs only. Also,
$$|R\cap C|=12,\quad |C\cap F\cap R|=|F^{\mathrm c}|\quad\text{and}\quad |F\cap R|>|F\cap C|.$$
A student is selected at random. Find the probability that the student studies both classical and folk.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the number in all three sets, $y$ the number in classical and folk only, and $z$ the number in folk and rock only. The classical-and-rock-only region contains $12-x$ students. Since everyone buys at least one category, the outside region contains 0.

The students outside $F$ are in classical only, rock only, or classical and rock only:
$$\begin{align*}x&=1+5+(12-x)\\2x&=18\\x&=9.\end{align*}$$
The seven disjoint regions total 28:
$$\begin{align*}28&=1+9+5+(12-9)+9+y+z\\y+z&=1.\end{align*}$$
The inequality $|F\cap R|>|F\cap C|$ gives $9+z>9+y$, so $z>y$. As region counts are non-negative integers, $y=0$ and $z=1$.
$$\begin{align*}|C\cap F|&=9+0\\|C\cap F|&=9\\P(C\cap F)&=\frac{9}{28}.\end{align*}$$
